purpose: Defines the six-phase workflow that turns a requirements document into UX/UI design outputs: design tokens, component visual specs and a UX evaluation, driven by a Design Intent.
summary: Positioning of the skill between requirements and technical design, with inputs (requirements with ASCII screen specs) and outputs (THEME, CMP, UXEVAL documents)
Context management: per-phase knowledge retrieval via rules query, resident design philosophy, no agent isolation
Phase 1: loading requirements, organizing screens/components/functions, collecting reference designs, fetching rule documents
Phase 2.0: acquiring and confirming Design Intent (experience, tension axis, distinctiveness, references, anti-goals, signature) and branching of later phases
Phase 2: direction decision covering personality analysis, brand tension axis, cultural references, provocations, recommendation and confirmation
Phase 3: design token creation (colors with Light/Dark, typography, spacing, radius/shadow, signature tokenization, quality checklist)
Phase 4: converting ASCII layouts into component visual specs, naming, platform states (iOS/macOS), UX notes, signature placement check
Phase 5: UX self-evaluation using Norman three levels, Rams principles, HIG/Nielsen/Gestalt, distinctiveness and memorability metrics, summary format
Phase 6: generating THEME/CMP/UXEVAL files, AI review, specs index update, commit confirmation, completion guidance
Dialogue principles (visual presentation, rationale, diverge-select-concretize, no bland defaults) and anti-pattern table
tasks: Creating visual design from a requirements document
Designing design tokens (colors, typography, spacing, radius)
Determining Design Intent and design direction
Evaluating UX quality of a created design system
Editing or reviewing the start-uxui-design skill workflow
title: UX/UI デザイン創造ワークフロー
